name: Jaunde
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Heepe, Martin (ed.). 1919. Jaunde-Texte von Karl Atangana und Paul Messi, nebst experimentalphonetischen Untersuchungen über die Tonhöhen im Jaunde und einer Einführung in die Jaundesprache. (Abhandlungen des Hamburgischen Kolonialinstituts 24.) Hamburg: L. Friederichsen. Corroborated by Nekes, P. Hermann. 1911. Lehrbuch der Jaunde-Sprache. (Lehrbücher des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin 26.) Berlin: Georg Reimer.
catalog_locator: Heepe 1919, 'Einführung in die Jaundesprache', section 'Die Laute des Jaunde und ihre Bezeichnung, a. Vokale', p. 152; Nekes 1911 §19 'Der dynamische Akzent', p. 26, and §15 pp. 22-23.
catalog_quote: Wichtiger als Länge und Kürze ist der dynamische Akzent, also die Unterscheidung von betonten und unbetonten Silben, die nicht zu verwechseln ist mit der Tonhöhe. Jede Silbe hat ihre Tonhöhe, nämlich hoch oder tief; hier aber handelt es sich um Betonung, ob stark oder schwach; also um den Starkton. Der Starkton oder dynamische Akzent ruht im Jaunde, soweit er überhaupt mit Sicherheit zu beobachten ist, auf der Stammsilbe eines Wortes, bezw. wenn man auch zweisilbige Stämme annimmt, auf der ersten Stammsilbe. Bei den Verben rückt er im unverkürzten Imperativ auf die Endsilbe. Der Anfänger tut gut, um sich zunächst die unentbehrliche Beherrschung der Tonhöhen zu verschaffen, vom Starkton gänzlich abzusehen und gar nichts zu betonen, sondern nur auf Hoch- und Tiefton der Silben zu achten [Heepe 1919: 152]. ... Wie schon bemerkt, ist der dynamische Akzent oder Starkton unabhängig von der Höhe des musikalischen Tones; z. B. in dem Worte afogólo Hut, ruht der Starkton auf der zweiten tieftonigen Silbe, nicht auf der dritten hochtonigen. Genaue Gesetze über den dynamischen Akzent lassen sich nicht aufstellen. In der Regel ist die erste Stammsilbe akzentuiert. Die übrigen Silben sind oft so schwach akzentuiert, daß ihre Vokale kaum mehr vom reduzierten ę zu unterscheiden sind [Nekes 1911: 26].

new_statements.translation: More important than length and shortness is the dynamic accent, i.e. the distinction of stressed and unstressed syllables, which is not to be confused with pitch. Every syllable has its pitch, namely high or low; here however it is a matter of stress, whether strong or weak; that is, the stress accent (Starkton). In Jaunde the stress or dynamic accent rests, insofar as it can be observed with certainty at all, on the stem syllable of a word, or, if one also assumes disyllabic stems, on the first stem syllable. In verbs it moves to the final syllable in the unshortened imperative.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ewondo is a tone language with a separate, weak dynamic (stress) accent that falls on the (first) syllable of the stem/root, independent of tone and of prefixes; Nekes 1911 §19 independently states the same default ('In der Regel ist die erste Stammsilbe akzentuiert'), adding that stress is independent of tone height and that unstressed vowels reduce toward schwa.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; Nekes 1911 notes remaining syllables are so weakly stressed their vowels approach reduced schwa.
new_statements.exceptions: Heepe: in verbs the stress shifts to the final syllable in the unshortened imperative. Nekes 1911 §19: 'Genaue Gesetze über den dynamischen Akzent lassen sich nicht aufstellen' (exact laws cannot be set up), stem-initial is the rule 'in der Regel'; §15 stress can also be used for emphasis of words in the sentence without changing tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (Stammsilbe eines Wortes); both authors hedge that the stress accent is weak/hard to observe relative to tone. The modern grammar (Redden 1979) posits only tones and junctures as suprasegmentals and makes no stress statement; Essono 1993/2000 could not be consulted.
new_statements.identity_note: 'Jaunde' (Nekes 1911, 1913; Heepe 1919) is the German colonial name for Ewondo (Yaoundé), i.e. the same language ewon1239; Heepe's speakers were Karl Atangana and Paul Messi (Ewondo of Yaoundé). Redden 1979 describes the idiolect of one speaker from Yaoundé-Eturi. No dialect mismatch.

tone_statements.quote: 1. Das Jaunde ist eine Tonsprache, für die die Unterscheidung zweier Tonlagen wesentlich ist, wie das in meiner Arbeit,, Jaunde-Toxto" des näheren ausgeführt ist. … Unter- scheidung lediglich zweier Tonstufen unter Hinzunahme rhythmischer Unterscheidungen der Zeitfolge … der Begriff ,, Krieg" Nr. 45 vermittelt, indem man das Jaundewort für Krieg hitd nach seinen Ton- elementen, einem Tief- und einem Hochton, trommelt. … bezeichnet der Akut (') Hochton, Akut mit Gravis (^) Hoch- tiefton, Gravis mit Akut (^) Tiefhochton. tone_statements.translation: 1. Jaunde is a tone language for which the distinction of two pitch levels is essential, as is set out in detail in my work 'Jaunde-Texte'. … distinction of merely two tone levels with the addition of rhythmic distinctions of timing … the notion 'war', No. 45, is conveyed by drumming the Jaunde word for war, bitá, according to its tone elements, a low and a high tone. … the acute (´) marks high tone, acute with grave (^) high-low tone, grave with acute (ˇ) low-high tone. Low tone is left unmarked.

tone_statements.summary: Jaunde is a tone language with two essential pitch levels, high and low (high-low, low-high written as double tones); drum signals follow the spoken tones exactly; Nekes's third mid tone is queried.

tone_statements.citation: Nekes, P. Hermann. 1911. Die Bedeutung des musikalischen Tones in den Bantusprachen. Anthropos 6: 546-574. (Sections I-IV: Bantu languages as tone languages, origin of the tones, transcription, and the grammatical/lexical functions of tone, worked out 'hauptsaechlich' on Jaunde [= Ewondo] with Schambala comparisons.)
tone_statements.quote: Als Grundténe fand ich nur Tief- und Hochton ... Der Tiefton des Jaunde wird unwillkiirlich etwas héher ausgesprochen, also als Mittelton, sobald er zwischen Hocht6nen steht. ... Alle anderen vorkommenden Tone sind Kontraktionszeichen, so der steigende Ton, Tiefhochton (bzw. Mittelhochton nach der obigen Regel), der fallende Ton, Hochtiefton (bzw. Hochmittelton), sowie der dem Jaunde cigene emphatische Mittelton, der nur als Finalton auf der Endsilbe eines Wortes stehen kann. Dieser Mittelton ist an dem starken, kurz abgebrochenen Druck (dynamischer Akzent), von dem er stets begleitet ist, leicht erkenntlich ... [p. 552:] Im Jaunde liegt der Starkton auf der ersten Stammsilbe.
tone_statements.translation: As basic tones I found only low and high tone ... The low tone of Jaunde is involuntarily pronounced somewhat higher, i.e. as a mid tone, as soon as it stands between high tones. ... All other tones that occur are signs of contraction: the rising tone, low-high (or mid-high by the above rule), the falling tone, high-low (or high-mid), and the emphatic mid tone peculiar to Jaunde, which can stand only as a final tone on the last syllable of a word. This mid tone is easily recognised by the strong, abruptly cut-off pressure (dynamic accent) that always accompanies it ... [p. 552:] In Jaunde the stress (Starkton) lies on the first stem syllable.
tone_statements.locator: p. 550, section II 'Entstehung der Toene', para. 10 (tone inventory); p. 552, section III, para. 14 (Starkton on the first stem syllable); article pp. 546-574
tone_statements.summary: Two basic level tones, High and Low, every syllable tone-bearing (syllable as TBU); Low realised as Mid between Highs (allotonic); contour tones Rising (LH) and Falling (HL) analysed as products of syllable contraction; an additional 'emphatic Mittelton' restricted to word-final position, always co-occurring with a strong short dynamic accent, forming LM and HM contours; measured intervals L-M c.…

tone_statements.citation: Redden, James E. 1979. A Descriptive Grammar of Ewondo (clean print copy; archive.org descriptivegramm0000redd, controlled digital lending)
tone_statements.quote: 1.1.3. There are 3 tone phonemes: high /´/, mid /¯/, and low /`/. Low is not marked except on syllabic nasals, in order to distinguish initial syllabic nasal plus consonant from initial clusters of nasal plus consonant. All vowels and syllabic nasals have tone, but syllabic nasals lose their tone after a vowel. [...] 1.5. The 3 tones of Ewondo are relative, i.e. the distances between the tones are not constant, exact musical intervals. The interval between high and mid is about a musical third, i.e. a difference of one note on the piano. [...] The interval between mid and low is usually somewhat greater than the interval between high and mid. Ewondo is a terraced-tone language, i.e. intonation occurs with syllable tone to give a decreasing interval between high and low. After a low, a high is lower than the previous high by the same interval as a mid. [...] Thus, it can be seen that if a syllable with low tone is elided or omitted the down-stepped high is the same as a mid. No doubt this is the origin of mid tone. Mid tone occurs only after a high or a mid. After a low, there are only two choices: remain on the same level, i.e., remain low; or rise to a higher level, i.e., rise to

sources.citation: Redden, James E. 1979. A Descriptive Grammar of Ewondo. (Occasional Papers on Linguistics 4.) Carbondale: Department of Linguistics, Southern Illinois University. [ERIC ED185833 microfiche scan]
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Phonology p.5: 'Ewondo has 33 phonemes: 27 segmentals and 6 suprasegmentals.. suprasegmentals are divided into 3 tones and 3 junctures'; §1.1.3-1.1.4 (p.6) describe high/mid/low tone and three junctures; no stress or accent phoneme is posited and no statement on prominence appears (only 'sentence stress' in English glosses).

sources.citation: Owona, Antoine (2004). L'orthographe harmonisée de l'ewondo. Yaoundé. Université de Yaoundé I. 112 pp.
sources.note: An orthography thesis: reviews the German (Nekes), French (Pichon), Tsala, Abega and Essono writing systems and proposes tone marking, vowel-length and word-division rules. Full-text search of the (noisy) text for accent/accentu/intensité/tonique/dynamique/Betonung/stress finds nothing about word stress; it neither confirms nor denies the Heepe/Nekes dynamic-accent statement already on record.

sources.citation: Nekes, Hermann. 1913. Die Sprache der Jaunde in Kamerun. (Deutsche Kolonialsprachen 5.) Berlin: Reimer.
sources.note: Only incidental: p.7 the middle vowel of a trisyllabic word and the unaccented final vowel of a word often reduce to schwa; no explicit rule for accent placement found.

tone.summary: Two basic level tones, High and Low, every syllable tone-bearing (syllable as TBU); Low realised as Mid between Highs (allotonic); contour tones Rising (LH) and Falling (HL) analysed as products of syllable contraction; an additional 'emphatic Mittelton' restricted to word-final position, always co-occurring with a strong short dynamic accent, forming LM and HM contours; measured intervals L-M c.…
tone.says: Every word and syllable of Jaunde has a fixed tone; two basic tones, low and high; low is raised to mid between highs (non-distinctive, ignored on the drum); rising (low-high) and falling (high-low) tones are contraction products; a Jaunde-specific emphatic final mid tone, only word-final, always accompanied by a strong short dynamic stress, combinable into low-mid and high-mid; pitch intervals L-M about 1.5-2 tones, M-H 0.5-0.75 tone; dynamic stress (Starkton) lies on the first stem syllable a…
